findings.description: Tool combination enables command injection. Agent can run shell commands — host compromise via prompt injection.
findings.impact: Successful prompt injection on this agent results in: command injection.
findings.remediation: Add policy guards between tools. Require user confirmation for cross-domain tool sequences. Apply principle of least privilege per tool.

findings.description: Tool description contains language that could hijack the agent: 'override'.
findings.impact: Tool descriptions are added to the LLM context. Imperative language can override the agent's intended behaviour.
findings.remediation: Sanitise tool descriptions. Use neutral, declarative language. Never load tool descriptions from untrusted sources.

findings.description: Chain of tools 'override' + '__call__' enables arbitrary tool request tampering, handler hijacking, and execution control flow manipulation.
findings.evidence: Tool 'override' permits replacing tool execution requests with arbitrary new payloads, while '__call__' exposes low-level interception and invocation control over tool handlers.
findings.impact: An agent or prompt injection attack can leverage these capabilities to bypass authorization checks, modify parameters of sensitive tools, redirect tool execution paths, and achieve unauthorized execution privilege escalation within the model context environment.
findings.remediation: Remove low-level metaprogramming and execution-interception functions ('__call__', 'override') from the toolset exposed to the agent. Enforce authorization, validation, and execution controls centrally within the host platform rather than exposing primitive invocation controls to the LLM runtime.

findings.description: Chain of tools _create_stdio_session + __call__ enables arbitrary local command execution and data exfiltration.
findings.evidence: Tool '_create_stdio_session' executes arbitrary local commands, while tool '__call__' creates an HTTP client capable of making outbound network requests.
findings.impact: An attacker capable of influencing agent tool calls could leverage '_create_stdio_session' to execute system commands (reading local files, environment variables, or credentials) and use '__call__' or network session creators to exfiltrate the collected data to an external server.
findings.remediation: Restrict or sandbox '_create_stdio_session' using a strict command allowlist or containerized environment, implement strict network egress filtering/domain allowlists for network tools, and require explicit human confirmation prior to executing shell commands.

attack_paths.description: Agent can run shell commands — host compromise via prompt injection.
